title: Embedding quantization profile validation and similarity-regression gating
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: We need repeatable, auditable quantization profiles for embedding models (INT8 and FP16 targets) that preserve end-to-end similarity behavior. Recent ad-hoc quant sweeps produced variants with acceptable token-level MSE but unexplained cosine-similarity regressions on production corpora. This ticket scopes a calibration + validation workflow and a safety gate (similarity-regression gating) to prevent regressions from rolling out to hosted customers.

Goals:
- Define per-model quantization profile artifacts (cal profiles) that include per-layer scaling parameters and fallback metadata.
- Implement an automated calibration workflow that produces deterministic profiles from calibration corpora and stores metadata (dataset fingerprints, seed, toolchain version).
- Validate profile quality via multi-metric checks: corpus-wise cosine similarity distributions, top-k nearest-neighbor recall (k=10), and a semantic-search MRR proxy.
- Add a gating criterion that blocks rollout when similarity regressions exceed thresholds and surface clear diagnostics in Console.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Calibration harness: a reproducible runner that takes a model checkpoint, calibration corpus(s), and quant target (INT8/FP16/FP8 optional) and outputs a profile tarball + metadata JSON. Support deterministic seeds and GPU/CPU modes.
2) Validation suite: batch job that computes baseline vs quantized embedding similarity histograms for multiple corpora (internal bench, customer-simulated, random crawls). Produce KS-test p-values, mean/median cosine deltas, and percentile deltas (1/5/50/95/99).
3) Regression gate: a simple rules engine that checks the validation outputs and emits PASS/FLAG/FAIL with structured reasons. Rules initial proposal: mean cosine drop <= 0.01, 95th percentile drop <= 0.03, top-k recall change <= 1.5% absolute.
4) Console integration: dashboard widgets showing per-profile calibration artifacts, distribution overlays, and a one-click rollback to unquantized model.
5) Alerts and monitoring: automated daily drift checks (KS test and percentile checks) for deployed quantized variants; PagerDuty only on high-impact customers.

Why this differs from prior tickets: previous docs centered on embedding calibration experiments and drift detectors; this ticket fuses a formal artifact format for quant profiles with gateable validation criteria and the operational integration needed for safe rollouts.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Stricter gates reduce rollout velocity; loosen them too much and customer quality degrades. We'll start conservative and iterate.
- Calibration corpora selection matters — overfitting to bench corpora can produce optimistic metrics. We'll use multiple corpora and explicit corpus fingerprints.
- FP16 vs INT8 tradeoff: INT8 yields larger cost wins but higher variance on tail corpora; profiles must include a "confidence band" and fallbacks to FP16 for customers with strict SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces reproducible profile artifact (sha256) and metadata for a given seed and corpus set.
Validation suite runs as CI job and reports KS p-values + percentile deltas; sample job output committed to artifacts/ENG-33456/validate-run-001.json.
Regressions gate evaluates to PASS/FLAG/FAIL and blocks canary rollout when status==FAIL.
Console dashboard displays overlayed cosine distributions for baseline vs quantized for at least three corpora.
Runbook created for on-call: how to triage flagged quant profiles and steps to rollback or create a mitigation profile.

notes: Calibration corpora set: internal-bench-v2, customer-sim-augmented, web-sample-2025Q4; each corpus will be fingerprinted (sha256 list) and referenced in profile metadata.
Validation metrics to export: mean cosine, median cosine, 1/5/50/95/99 percentile deltas, KS p-value, top-k recall@10, semantic MRR proxy computed via 10 canonical queries.
Gating thresholds are initial and will be tuned after 2 weeks of canary data. We'll adopt conservative thresholds for customers with >$5k/month spend.

Profile artifact name convention: <model>-<quant>-<profile-sha>.tar.gz; metadata file profile.json includes: model_sha, quant_scheme, layers_calibrated, corpus_fingerprints, seed, toolchain_version, created_by.
Fallback behavior: when gate FAIL, route to unquantized variant or FP16 depending on customer SLA tier. Implement routing knob in smart router service with per-customer policy.
